newsitem.title: USA: Tosco turns back 40,000 bpd crude - traders.
newsitem.headline: Tosco turns back 40,000 bpd crude - traders.

text.p: Tosco Corp reportedly declined three current deliveries of California heavy crude oil late Monday, due to throttled back production at its Martinez, Calif. refinery, traders said Tuesday.
"Tosco declared force majeure on roughly 40,000 barrels-per-day," a trader said.

Company officials declined comment but a union official on Monday said a fire at the plant's hydrocracker last week "certainly reduced (crude) capacity," at the 156,000 bpd facility, and may have cut 20,000 bpd of gasoline output.
The unit, shut since the fire, could remain down for eight to 10 weeks, according to a union official at the plant.
The plant's scaled back production comes at a time when at least two other refiners in the region have extra heavy crude in storage because of maintenance on production units.
"It puts a lot of supply out there and there's not a lot of demand," a trader said.
Traders said if Tosco sells, the excess supply would likely drag down a market already flooded with supply.
"It don't know how far it could go," a trader said.
The posted average price for Kern River, a representative heavy grade, has fallen $1.50 to $18.00 a barrel since early January.
Traders, who buy heavy grade at a discount off postings, have recently bought cargoes at 50 to 25 cents off the average, about a 15 cent drop since earlier this month.
